title: Six-Month Outcomes of Accelerated Corneal Cross-Linking with a Total Dose of 7.2 J/cm2 Using Dextran-Free Riboflavin

license.statement: CC BY-NC 4.0 (article <license-p>: Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/)

groups.description: 42 eyes of 35 patients with progressive keratoconus (Kmax increase of at least 1.00 D over the past year); epithelium-off accelerated CXL with dextran-free 0.1% riboflavin with HPMC (VibeX Rapid) for 10 minutes, then UVA 12 mW/cm2 for 10 minutes (7.2 J/cm2, KXL System); prospective, single arm; age 24.7 +/- 4.2 years, range 18-32

series.notes: mean ± SD (Table 1 footnote); unit D in the row label; Pentacam (Oculus) Scheimpflug, mean of three measurements per Methods; column 'Postoperative 6 months'; per-visit n not reported (42 eyes)

notes: Age group mixed: the reported age range 18-32 years includes patients aged 18 (18 years or younger) and older than 18.
Single-arm study of a commercial accelerated protocol without a declared experimental arm: role control.

Table 1 also gives UDVA, CDVA, spherical power, cylindrical power, spherical equivalent, flat and steep keratometry, central corneal thickness and endothelial cell density; demarcation line depth is reported in the text (not extracted).
